cards.explanation: The answer is a pair of sandals. The LORD says they sell "…the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals." I think a pair of sandals is a small price, friends, and that makes the charge sting even more.

The answer is True. The LORD says a man and his father have relations with the same girl "…and so profane My holy name." That's heavy, so I'll just say it plainly. The LORD says it touches His holy name.
The answer is fines. The LORD says that in the house of their God, they drink "…wine obtained through fines." It's one of the charges He brings against Israel, and I think it's a heavy one, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "…it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them…" and the Amorite was tall, "…like that of the cedars…" Israel didn't win by being bigger, friends. He did it, from the fruit above to the roots below.

The answer is Egypt. The LORD says, "…I brought you up from the land of Egypt…" He's reminding Israel of what He did for them. That's quite a list of reminders, friends, and it's only getting started.

The answer is forty. The LORD says He "…led you forty years in the wilderness…" He led them the whole way, and the goal was that they might take possession of the land of the Amorite. Forty years is a long road, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "…you made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets not to prophesy." The prophets were the ones He raised up, and Israel told them to stop. They told them to hush.
The answer is their escape. The LORD says, "Escape will fail the swift…" The swift are named right there in verse 14, friends, next to the strong and the mighty.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "…the horseman will not save his life." He's listed in verse 15 along with the archer and the fleet of foot. So the horseman doesn't get away either, friends. The LORD also says that on that day even the bravest of mighty men will flee naked (Amos 2:16).
The answer is flee naked. The LORD says, "Even the bravest of mighty men will flee naked on that day…" Bravest is the word He uses, friends, and even they flee.
